# ReviewFn

> Evidence-backed advisory pull request reviews, isolated execution, and report contracts.

This file concatenates the full text of every documentation page so it can be loaded into
an LLM-based assistant in a single shot. For a page index, see https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/static/llms.txt.

# Documentation

<!-- page:docs:getting-started.md path:/docs/getting-started -->
# Getting started

> Install ReviewFn and run a local advisory review.


ReviewFn requires Node.js 22 or newer, Git, a supported Codex CLI, and Docker for approved tests. Install the CLI as a development dependency in the repository being reviewed:

```sh
npm install --save-dev @superfunctions/reviewfn-cli
npx reviewfn init
npx reviewfn preflight --base origin/main --head HEAD --issue ENG-123
npx reviewfn review --base origin/main --head HEAD --issue ENG-123
```

`init` creates versioned `.reviewfn/config.json` and `.reviewfn/policy.json`. Review and edit them before running inference. `preflight` checks adapter, harness, model/auth, Docker, policy, and context compatibility. `review` captures committed revisions and writes `.reviewfn/output/report.json`, `.reviewfn/output/report.md`, and content-addressed evidence under `.reviewfn/output/artifacts` (or `<output>/artifacts` when `--output` is set). Ignore generated output and artifacts in the consumer repository.

The local CLI also supports `render --input report.json` and `evaluate --input evaluation.json`. `publish` is a separate command for a trusted GitHub job. The [CLI source](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/cli/src/main.ts) lists the current flags. Use [configuration](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/configuration.md) for adapters, model authentication, test argv, and retention settings.

For a setup without connected services, use only the `repository-markdown` context adapter. For Linear, configure `composio-linear` with an explicit account, expected workspace, and issue key. Never put credential values into the config files; `credentialEnv` records an environment variable name.

---

<!-- page:docs:index.md path:/docs -->
# ReviewFn

> Evidence-backed advisory pull request review.


ReviewFn reviews a frozen base/head change against issue and repository context. It runs approved tests in a disposable, isolated checkout, asks a compatible review harness for structured assessments, validates citations and evidence, and produces an advisory report. A separate trusted job can publish one current-head summary and a neutral GitHub check.

The first release is advisory. It does not edit code, push, merge, or declare a passing review when context, execution, evidence, or head identity is incomplete. Start with the [CLI quick start](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md), follow the [review workflow](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/workflow.md), and configure the [security boundary](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/security.md) before reviewing untrusted PRs.

The detailed [configuration](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/configuration.md), [report schema](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/report-schema.md), [GitHub Action](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/github-action.md), and [evaluation](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/evaluation.md) pages mirror the source guides on the [`dev` branch](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/tree/dev/reviewfn/docs). They describe the current `dev` contract; verify the installed package version before assuming an earlier release has the same behavior.

---

<!-- page:docs:operations-and-limits.md path:/docs/operations-and-limits -->
# Operations and limits

> Deployment gates, retention, and evidence boundaries.


ReviewFn's release gate runs package suites, Docker containment cases, Action shell-input tests, and an external installed CLI pipeline. Docker images, Composio/Linear access, GitHub publication credentials, and the inference proxy need explicit setup. Local docs validation cannot prove those hosted systems.

The output is advisory. A `ready` verdict requires complete coverage and validated evidence; it is not a merge authorization. Required GitHub checks need a later calibrated policy and release. The publisher uses a neutral check and one profile summary for the exact reviewed head.

ReviewFn retains content-addressed artifacts and redacted logs. Transcripts require explicit `retainTranscript: true`. The CLI applies retention cleanup when saving a new run. Idle stores need scheduled `FileArtifactStore.deleteExpired()`, and an ambiguous retention or publication lock requires operator verification before removal. See [security details](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/security.md).

Evaluation examples in the repository include retrospective, agent-labeled and limited live receipts. They are schema and integration evidence, not a held-out model quality estimate. Review [evaluation](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/evaluation.md) before using these numbers to choose a model or policy.

---

<!-- page:docs:packages.md path:/docs/packages -->
# Packages

> Choose the ReviewFn package for each integration layer.


| Package | Consumer responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `@superfunctions/reviewfn-cli` | `reviewfn` binary for init, preflight, review, render, publish, and evaluate. |
| `@superfunctions/reviewfn-core` | Versioned contracts, identity, policy, coordinator, validation, artifacts, and rendering. |
| `@superfunctions/reviewfn-harness-codex` | Supported Codex CLI capability checks, bounded execution, and structured output normalization. |
| `@superfunctions/reviewfn-context-composio` | Explicit-account Linear issue, comment, and document context snapshots. |
| `@superfunctions/reviewfn-github` | Exact Git source snapshots and idempotent advisory GitHub publication. |
| `@superfunctions/reviewfn-testing` | Fakes, fixtures, replay metrics, and evaluation comparison checks. |

Each package is independently installable and has a separate `README.md`. The CLI depends on the other five packages. Import the lower-level packages when embedding ReviewFn in a trusted host, and preserve their identity, policy, and artifact boundaries. The [source package list](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/tree/dev/reviewfn) is the current implementation map.

---

<!-- page:docs:publication.md path:/docs/publication -->
# GitHub publication

> Keep review execution separate from trusted advisory publishing.


`reviewfn/github/action.yml` is a composite action for the credential-free review stage. Pin the action and CLI version, check out the exact head with full history and no persisted credentials, and supply trusted base/head/PR identity. The review job uploads its report and artifacts. Public forks require an explicitly provisioned isolated proxy runner.

In a separate trusted job, download only the artifact from that review job and run:

```sh
reviewfn publish --input "$REPORT" --repository "$REPOSITORY" \
  --pull-request "$PR_NUMBER" --head "$EXPECTED_HEAD" --profile requirements
```

The action's `report` output names the artifact directory, not a file: set `REPORT` to the `report.json` file inside the downloaded artifact. Derive the other values from trusted workflow metadata, not the report artifact. The publisher needs GitHub write permissions for PR comments and checks and must not execute PR code. Use one repository/PR/profile concurrency group. Publication rechecks the current head before writes, maintains a single profile summary, and updates the same run's check idempotently. A head change during a GitHub write can leave a clearly labeled older-head comment; the next run replaces it.

Checks remain neutral regardless of verdict. Version 0.1 does not support a `gate` output mode. The [full GitHub Action guide](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/github-action.md) gives permissions, pinning, retries, lease recovery, and publisher-login details.

---

<!-- page:docs:reference/configuration.md path:/docs/reference/configuration -->
# Configuration contract

> Versioned config, policy, adapter selection, and execution limits.


ReviewFn uses versioned JSON files at `.reviewfn/config.json` and `.reviewfn/policy.json`. Unknown adapters fail preflight. Secret values never belong in either file; `credentialEnv` names an environment variable without recording its value.

In GitHub Actions, pass `--trusted-config-from-base`. ReviewFn reads both files using `git show BASE:path`, so a pull request cannot weaken the policy controlling its own review.

The configuration selects the profile, harness, inference provider/model/auth, context adapters, approved argv test commands, outputs and retention. Commands are argv arrays and never pass through a shell. Profiles contain 1–80 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens so accepted configurations remain publishable. Optional context identities must be nonempty strings when present.

`composio-linear` requires:

- `account`: explicit Composio account alias, word ID, or connected-account ID;
- `expectedWorkspace`: expected Linear organization/team identity;
- `issue`: key such as `ENG-123`.

`repository-markdown` accepts exact repository-relative paths or `**/*.md` suffix patterns. Traversal and symlink escapes are refused.

Fallback entries are provenance only. ReviewFn never selects one automatically; an operator must explicitly rerun a compatible configuration.

Version 0.1 accepts only `advisory` output mode. Both configuration and policy validation reject `gate`; required-check behavior needs a later, separately calibrated and authorized release.

PR inference requires a trusted Docker image and action-proxy authentication with an explicit model. Local API-key and ChatGPT modes are restricted to trusted repositories. `local-isolated` names the mandatory Docker execution adapter; other adapter names fail preflight. Test commands use container paths such as `node`, not a host-specific executable path. See the security model for fixed resource bounds. `retainTranscript` is false unless explicitly enabled. Normalized events retain only bounded telemetry counters, never message, reasoning or tool-output payloads; content-bearing JSONL belongs to the separately retained opt-in transcript.

Linear comment and document connection requests share a request budget equal to the configured context source limit. Empty pages consume that budget; exhaustion records incomplete context. The prompt lists policy-authorized source IDs explicitly, excluding comments when their authority is disabled.

---

<!-- page:docs:reference/evaluation.md path:/docs/reference/evaluation -->
# Evaluation contract

> Measure frozen cases and report comparison confounds.


`reviewfn evaluate --input evaluation.json` consumes frozen cases and observed outcomes. Each case records source/change digests, agent-authored requirements, known gaps, valid findings, acceptability, retrospective status and limitations.

The result always includes numerators and denominators for requirement-extraction recall, gap-detection recall, finding precision, false-block rate, evidence validity and completion rate. Failed and missing outcomes remain in completion denominators. The false-block denominator includes only acceptable cases with an observed outcome; when none exist, the rate is null rather than zero. Runtime, tokens and measurable cost are reported only when observed; unavailable values remain null.

Comparisons name every changed harness, version, provider, model, prompt, context or budget dimension. A result with more than one changed dimension is confounded and must not be described as a model-only ranking.

Historical cases require exact contemporaneous heads and source snapshots. When source version history cannot be recovered, mark the case retrospective. Prior bot labels and assistant judgments are candidate labels, not adjudicated ground truth.

The repository includes `evaluation/data6-pr153.json` and its evidence ledger as a first retrospective schema smoke test. It must not be presented as model-quality evidence: it contains one agent-authored case, current rather than contemporaneous Linear source content, and no token, cost, or live-model timing observations.

`evaluation/data6-pr153-live.json` records a real Codex CLI 0.145.0 / gpt-5.6-sol run over bounded historical source excerpts, including eight extracted requirements, assessments, evidence, runtime and observed usage. It is separate from the older agent-labeled schema smoke. The source summary is retrospective, the downstream repository is absent, and no held-out or human-adjudicated model-quality estimate is claimed. `linear-live-receipt.json` records successful live retrieval of SFNS-3, four comments and three linked specifications by the actual Composio adapter. That receipt is a metadata-only observation, not a replayable content artifact: its digests cannot be independently recomputed from the committed receipt. The local historical CLI was 0.145.0; the separately tested container image pins 0.154.0.

The executable release gate runs the package suites, Docker containment cases, Action shell-input tests and an external installed CLI pipeline. `CONFORMANCE_FIXTURES` is a scenario catalog, not a count of executed tests. Use the gate's actual test output for coverage claims; platform-specific containment and external service availability remain explicit integration prerequisites.

---

<!-- page:docs:reference/github-action.md path:/docs/reference/github-action -->
# GitHub Action and publication

> Set up a credential-free review job and a separate trusted publisher.


The bundled composite is the credential-free review stage. It installs the pinned public CLI with lifecycle scripts disabled in a fresh runner-temporary directory, ignores checkout/user npm configuration, and invokes the installed entrypoint by absolute path while passing the checkout via --root. PR-local node_modules and executables cannot satisfy or shadow the launcher. Install the pinned CLI version, pull the pinned test image and build `reviewfn-codex:0.154.0` using the Dockerfile from the trusted harness package. Provision an inference-only Responses API proxy outside the untrusted review job. Set trusted base configuration to `action-proxy` with an explicit model, omit `harness.executable`, and provide an endpoint reachable from the Docker bridge.

Use `pull_request` opened/synchronize/reopened or a maintainer-authorized dispatch. Checkout the exact head with full history and `persist-credentials: false`. Pin the Action to a reviewed commit. The review job needs only `contents: read`; it must not contain `GITHUB_TOKEN` in its environment or credentials cached in the checkout. Input values are transported through environment variables to quoted argv, and versions/commit IDs are validated before invoking the installed CLI entrypoint with `node`.

Upload the caller-owned output directory with `actions/upload-artifact` and a unique PR/head/run name; pin that action, and `actions/download-artifact` in the publisher job, to reviewed commit SHAs as well. Include report JSON, rendered Markdown and its artifacts directory. Publish in a separate trusted job with `pull-requests: write`, `issues: write`, and `checks: write`, without checking out PR code. Pin/install the published CLI there, download only the artifact from the corresponding review job, and run:

```sh
reviewfn publish --input "$REPORT" --repository "$REPOSITORY" \
  --pull-request "$PR_NUMBER" --head "$EXPECTED_HEAD" --profile requirements
```

Provide these identity values from trusted workflow event metadata, not the artifact. Export the publication token only in this job. Use a workflow concurrency group such as `reviewfn-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}-requirements` with `cancel-in-progress: false`. This serializes publishers across machines; the API adapter also serializes concurrent callers in one process and takes an exclusive local filesystem lease across processes. A crashed lease is never stolen by timeout; verify its recorded process is dead before operator cleanup. A failed publish can rerun this command against the same artifact without inference.

Head changes detected before writes return stale. The comment includes the exact reviewed SHA; because GitHub lacks conditional comment writes tied to the current PR head, a change during a write can still leave a clearly labeled older-head comment. The next run replaces it. The single marker-scoped comment must belong to the configured publisher login (default `github-actions[bot]`). Oversized reports fail publication with a bounded error while the full local report is retained. Checks remain neutral regardless of verdict. Never configure them as a merge gate for version 0.1.

Public fork execution requires a deliberately provisioned isolated proxy runner. No unauthenticated failure becomes a passing review. Repository package publication itself remains a separate release operation; this PR does not publish npm packages or merge code.

For a PAT or GitHub App publisher, pass `--publisher-login` with the authenticated comment author login. The default is `github-actions[bot]`. The local lease is deliberately never stolen after a crash, including interruption before owner metadata is written; confirm no publisher is active before removing that lease.

The CLI preserves a named base ref as target-branch provenance. With SHA-only input it records `unknown` unless `--target-branch` or the Actions `GITHUB_BASE_REF` supplies the branch label; the reviewed commits remain separately pinned.

<!-- page:docs:reference/panel-report-schema.md path:/docs/reference/panel-report-schema -->
# Panel report schema

> Panel policy, slot identity, slot runs, panel findings, and the panel report.


A panel report records one ReviewFn panel run: several slots review the same frozen change, and their findings are combined by union. The panel contract lives in `@superfunctions/reviewfn-core` under `panel/`. Each document below has a JSON Schema (`panelPolicySchema`, `slotIdentitySchema`, `slotRunSchema`, `panelFindingSchema`, `panelReportSchema`, `lensOutputSchema`), TypeScript types, and a deterministic validator. The 0.1 `ReviewReport` v1 ([report schema](report-schema.md)) is unchanged. It is embedded as the panel's requirements report, and a 0.1 single-harness report validates exactly as before.

## Severity

Panel findings use the 0.1 `FindingSeverity`. Lens priorities map as P0 = `critical`, P1 = `high`, P2 = `medium`, P3 = `low`. A panel lens never emits `info`: the lens output schema excludes it, and the validator rejects it in panel findings with `REVIEWFN_PANEL_FINDING_INVALID`.

## Panel policy

`{ version: 1, slots, quorum: { stage1, stage2 }, requirementsSlot, maxConcurrentSlots?, incremental: "full" | "delta" }`. `requirementsSlot` names a stage-1 or stage-2 slot, or is `null` to skip requirement extraction. `maxConcurrentSlots` is 1–8, and 2 when absent. `panelPolicyDigest(policy)` is the canonical SHA-256 of the validated policy with that default applied; the report records it as `panelPolicyDigest`. Loading the policy and repository tightening belong to the panel orchestrator.

A slot is `{ id, stage: 1 | 2 | "verifier", harness: { adapter, version }, inference: { provider, model, auth, credentialEnv? }, lens, budget: { timeoutMs, maxOutputBytes } }`. Slot IDs match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` and are unique. As in 0.1, the model `configured` defers to the harness default.

## Slot identity and runs

A slot's identity is the tuple (harness adapter, harness-reported version, provider, resolved model, auth mode, credential fingerprint). The fingerprint is the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the credential value, or of the harness-reported account identity (`credentialFingerprint(value)`). The value itself is never recorded. The fingerprint is absent when neither was observed. `slotIdentityKey(identity)` compares identities. A run's harness adapter, provider and auth mode must equal its slot's. `harness.version` is the exact version the harness must report. A run that reports another version records that version truthfully, but it can never be `completed` or `collapsed`. This is a contract on whoever produces the report: such a run must be recorded as `failed` (or another terminal that does not count), and the validator rejects it otherwise, so a version drift cannot form a separate identity that escapes collapse.

Within one stage, slots with the same identity count once toward quorum. The run that counts is the first `completed` run of that identity in policy order. A later run of the same identity that would also complete is recorded as `collapsed`, so a `collapsed` run always follows a counted run of its identity in its stage. Runs that end any other way (`failed`, `canceled`, `quota_exhausted`, `timed_out`, `malformed` or `void`) neither count nor collapse: if the first slot of an identity fails, a later slot of that identity can still complete and count. A stage-2 slot may share a stage-1 identity, because stages have separate quorums. Collapse affects quorum only: a `collapsed` run succeeded with its own lens, its findings name it as their origin, and a collapsed verifier's verifications stand. Verifier slots collapse by identity in the same way, although they have no quorum.

A slot run is `{ slotId, identity, terminal, voidReasons, startedAt, finishedAt, outputArtifact?, outputDigest?, usage? }`. `terminal` is `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, `quota_exhausted`, `timed_out`, `malformed`, `void` or `collapsed`. A `void` run lists at least one reason, and no other terminal lists any:

- `model_mismatch`: the resolved model differs from a configured model other than `configured`. This takes precedence over every other outcome: whenever the harness reports a resolved model that differs, the run is `void` and its reasons include `model_mismatch`, even if it also failed or timed out. When the harness reports no resolved model, `identity.model` records the configured model.
- `workspace_mutated`: the slot changed its checkout.
- `disallowed_tool_use`: the harness reported a forbidden tool.

Usage values (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `costUsd`) appear only when the harness observed them. Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC with in-range fields. The validator also rejects dates that do not exist, such as February 30, and a run that finishes before it starts.

## Lens output

Lens slots return `{ findings, evidence, inspectedPaths, uninspected }`, which is the 0.1 harness output without requirements or assessments. The requirements slot keeps the full 0.1 harness schema. `HarnessInput.outputSchema` selects the structured-output schema for a run. The Codex adapter first compiles it as given with strict Ajv, then checks that it lies inside the provider strict subset that the lens and 0.1 harness schemas use (`unsupportedOutputSchema`). In that subset, the root is a `type: "object"` schema and is the only place for `$defs` or `definitions`. Object schemas have `type: "object"`, `properties`, `required` naming only those properties, and `additionalProperties: false`. Array schemas have `items`, `minItems` and `maxItems`. Scalar schemas have `type` (a list of scalar types may include `"null"`), `enum`, `const`, and string or number constraints. `anyOf` is a pure union and `$ref` points to a local `$defs` or `definitions` entry; neither takes another keyword. `description` and `title` may appear anywhere. Any other keyword or shape, such as `allOf`, `oneOf`, `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `minProperties` or `$async`, fails the run before inference with a message naming it, distinct from the message for a schema that does not compile. Codex receives the provider-strict form (`strictProviderSchema`). Conversion is node-local: every property of an object schema is required, and a property gets a null alternative only when its own object schema does not require it. `const` and `enum` literals are copied verbatim. A property the caller schema requires keeps the values its own schema allows, including null when that schema allows it; a null the provider form added means the property is absent. The raw output must satisfy the provider-strict schema, or the caller schema as given, and no null is removed before this check. Nulls are dropped only afterwards, from the normalized result, which has empty requirements and assessments and must still be a valid 0.1 harness payload. Without `outputSchema`, Codex behaves as in 0.1.

## Panel findings

A panel finding is a 0.1 `Finding` plus the following fields:

- `origins: [{ slotId, lens }]`: at least one, and each a stage-1 or stage-2 slot with that lens whose run is `completed` or `collapsed`.
- `confidence`: 0–1. It is informational and never used for gating.
- `ruleIds`.
- `verification?: { verdict: "confirmed" | "refuted" | "inconclusive", slotId, evidenceIds, onBase: "present" | "absent" | "not_checked", reason }`.
- `disposition: "reported" | "dropped" | "suppressed"`, with `dispositionReason` and, for suppression, `suppressionReference`.

Verification comes from a `verifier` slot with a `completed` or `collapsed` run whose identity differs from every origin slot's identity. A confirmed or refuted verdict cites evidence. A dropped finding requires a refuted verification. A suppressed finding requires a `suppressionReference`, which is checked like a 0.1 waiver: it must be a verifiable reference (a literal excerpt or a valid line range) to an available, accepted source in the frozen context, and that source must be one of the policy's `sourceAuthority.waiverAuthorities`. Dropped and suppressed findings both require a `dispositionReason`. Dropped and suppressed findings stay in the report, so nothing disappears silently. Panel findings are lifecycle `new` until prior-finding provenance exists. Fingerprints are unique; agreement between slots is recorded in `origins`. The report records at most `policy.limits.maxFindings` panel findings, counting reported, dropped and suppressed findings alike; the panel orchestrator may add a separate bound for the slot union.

## Panel report

The report is `{ schemaVersion: 1, kind: "reviewfn-panel", runId, createdAt, change, changeDetail?, contextManifestDigest?, panelPolicyDigest, slots, slotRuns, requirementsReport?, gateReceipts, evidence, findings, clusters, coverage, coverageReasons, verdict? }`.

- `contextManifestDigest` is the digest of the frozen context the run used. When a requirements report is present it must be equal to that report's digest, and it may be omitted. Source references are verified only against a supplied context with this digest (or the requirements report's). Without such a context they fail closed.
- `gateReceipts` are 0.1 test receipts from the trusted gates.
- `evidence` holds the 0.1 evidence items that panel findings and verifications cite. Each item is verified as in 0.1, and every check fails closed when the source control, context or artifact store it needs is not supplied:
  - Code anchors on findings and evidence follow the 0.1 commit rule (`anchorCommitChecker`). An anchor cites the reviewed head. It may cite the merge base only for a changed path that source control reports absent at head, and `changeDetail.since` only for a path the verified delta removed that is absent at head. One narrow allowance exists for on-base evidence: evidence cited by at least one verification whose `onBase` is `present` or `absent`, and by no finding and no verification whose `onBase` is `not_checked`, may anchor at the merge base on any path. Every anchor must then be confirmed by `sourceControl.verifyAnchor`. Without source control or with an empty `root`, source control is never called: only head anchors and on-base evidence pass the commit rule, and they still fail as unverifiable.
  - Diff evidence lies in the changed paths or the verified delta paths.
  - Source evidence cites a verifiable source in the frozen context.
  - Test evidence names exactly one gate receipt at the reviewed head.
  - Artifact evidence names the digest of a slot run's retained `outputArtifact`.
  - A reproduced finding needs a completed gate receipt at the reviewed head whose stdout and stderr artifacts match their digests in the artifact store.
- `clusters` are `{ id, findingFingerprints }`. A finding belongs to at most one cluster.
- `requirementsReport` comes from the run of the panel policy's `requirementsSlot`, as findings come from their origins. A `completed` or `collapsed` run must supply it, with execution `completed`. A run that ended any other way may supply a report that records its failure (execution other than `completed`), and no requirements report may exist without a run of that slot. The report's configuration names the slot's harness adapter and configured inference (provider, model, auth mode), and for a run that succeeded the slot's harness version. It must review the same change and change detail as the panel, and is validated with the 0.1 validator. Without it, the panel's own `changeDetail` is verified against its artifacts, and `changeDetail.since` is checked against head and merge base ancestry when source control can answer it, as in 0.1.
- Incomplete coverage states at least one reason.

`verdict` uses 0.1's derivation (`derivePanelVerdict`). It runs over the requirements report plus the reported panel findings; dropped and suppressed findings are excluded. Coverage is complete only if both the panel and the requirements report are complete. Without a requirements report no requirement was assessed, so the verdict is at most `needs_verification`. A requirements report whose run did not complete leaves the verdict absent, as in 0.1. Panel output stays advisory.

## Validation codes

`validatePanelReport(report, policy, { sourceControl?, root?, context?, artifacts?, panelPolicy? })` returns `{ valid, issues: [{ code, path, message }], verdict }`. `policy` is the 0.1 `ReviewPolicy` (blocking severities, source authority and limits). `panelPolicy` is the panel policy the run used: its digest must equal `panelPolicyDigest` and its slots the report's slots. It binds the requirements report to `requirementsSlot`, so without it a requirements report fails closed. Quorum and coverage derivation from slot runs belong to the panel orchestrator and are not checked here. `path` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, and the empty string `""` is the document root. Structural problems are reported alone. `validatePanelPolicy(policy)` checks a panel policy, including that `requirementsSlot` names a stage-1 or stage-2 slot. The codes form a closed set:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_SCHEMA` | The document does not match its JSON Schema, a timestamp is not a real time, the supplied panel policy is invalid or differs from the report's digest or slots, or a run contradicts its slot (harness adapter, provider or auth mode, a `completed` or `collapsed` run reporting another harness version, model mismatch not voided with `model_mismatch`, `model_mismatch` without a mismatch, finish before start). |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_SLOT_DUPLICATE` | A slot ID is declared twice, a slot has two runs, a second completed run of an identity in a stage is not collapsed, or a collapsed run has no earlier completed run of its identity in its stage. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_SLOT_UNKNOWN` | A run or verification names no such slot (`validatePanelPolicy` also reports an unknown `requirementsSlot`). |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_FINDING_INVALID` | `info` severity, more findings than `maxFindings`, a lifecycle other than `new`, a duplicate fingerprint or origin, missing, unknown or unverifiable evidence, unknown requirements, an unverified reproduction, an anchor whose commit the anchor rule above does not allow or that source control cannot confirm, or an invalid cluster. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_ORIGIN_UNKNOWN` | An origin is not a stage-1 or stage-2 slot with that lens whose run is `completed` or `collapsed`. Or the requirements report has no run of the bound panel policy's `requirementsSlot`, is absent although that run succeeded, or has an execution or configuration that contradicts that run and slot. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_VERIFICATION_INVALID` | The verifier is not a verifier slot with a `completed` or `collapsed` run, shares an origin slot's identity, or cites missing or unknown evidence. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_DISPOSITION_INVALID` | Dropped without a refuted verification, suppressed without a verifiable waiver-authority reference, a `suppressionReference` on a finding that is not suppressed, or dropped or suppressed without a reason. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_VERDICT_MISMATCH` | `verdict` differs from the derived verdict. |

Errors from the 0.1 checks keep their 0.1 meaning: `REVIEWFN_CHANGE_DETAIL_MISMATCH` and `REVIEWFN_SINCE_NOT_ANCESTOR` keep their codes, and every other 0.1 error, including a requirements report for a different change, change detail or context, is `REVIEWFN_REPORT_INVALID`. Calendar validity of timestamps is a validator check beyond the JSON Schema pattern. `panelStructureIssues(kind, value)` is the structural TypeScript mirror of each JSON Schema. The tests check that it agrees with Ajv on every fixture and on systematic structural variants of each fixture.

## Panel orchestration

`PanelCoordinator` runs a panel and produces one panel report. The 0.1 `ReviewCoordinator` still serves the single-harness review. Both use the same code paths for preflight, change capture (`prepareReview`), harness output validation and redaction (`normalizeHarnessOutput`), 0.1 report assembly (`assembleReviewReport`), and artifacts.

- **Policy loading.** `loadPanelPolicy({ root, base, head, trustedFromBase })` reads `.reviewfn/panel.json`. In CI, or with `--trusted-config-from-base`, the base revision's copy is required and trusted. A head copy that differs is applied with `applyRepositoryPanelPolicy`, and it may only tighten: raise quorums, add slots that give new lenses to a stage, harness and model pair the trusted policy already has (within that pair's budget), or lower budgets or `maxConcurrentSlots`. Trusted slots keep their IDs, fields and order; added slots follow them. Any other difference, such as a lower quorum, a removed slot, a changed model, lens, stage, `requirementsSlot` or `incremental`, is rejected with `REVIEWFN_PANEL_POLICY_WEAKENED`, which lists every weakening. A local run without `trustedFromBase` reads the working-tree copy.
- **One preparation.** One trusted preflight covers the panel policy, every lens (`LensRegistry`; this release ships only `general`), every slot's harness and authentication, the context adapters, execution and `since`. The run then does one change capture, one context fetch and one test execution. Every slot receives the same frozen context and test receipts (the report's `gateReceipts`).
- **Stages.** Stage-1 slots run first. Stage-2 slots then always run, whatever stage 1 found, and their prompt lists every stage-1 finding as `stage1Findings` (possibly none) with the instruction to look for what stage 1 missed. Verifier slots are not run in this release; preflight warns `REVIEWFN_PANEL_VERIFIER_DEFERRED`.
- **Isolation.** Each slot runs in its own checkout: a `--shared` clone of the run's repository at the head commit, with no remote, no hooks, and attributes that keep the checked-out files byte-identical to the head blobs. After the slot finishes, the checkout's files are hashed through a run-owned Git directory (the slot's own `.git` is never consulted) and compared with the head tree. Directories the head lacks are also detected. Any difference, or a comparison that cannot complete, voids the slot with `workspace_mutated`, and the other slots' results stand. The checkout is removed after success, failure, timeout, cancellation and a harness that ignores abort. A harness that escapes its workspace on the host, or another local process changing a checkout during a run, is out of scope.
- **Budgets.** A slot's timeout is the smaller of `budget.timeoutMs` and the policy's `harnessTimeoutMs`. It starts once the slot's checkout exists. Its output limit is the smaller of `budget.maxOutputBytes` and `maxOutputBytes`. Both are passed to the harness. Exceeding either gives `timed_out`. Each stage is bounded by `harnessTimeoutMs`: a slot still running at the stage deadline, or still queued, is `timed_out`. Panel wall time is therefore bounded by `harnessTimeoutMs` times the number of stages, plus the harness abort grace and checkout cleanup. At most `maxConcurrentSlots` slots run at once.
- **Slot outcomes.** A served model other than the configured model voids the run with `model_mismatch`; a reported forbidden tool voids it with `disallowed_tool_use`. A harness reporting another version than the slot pins is `failed`. `quota_exhausted`, `failed`, `malformed`, `timed_out`, `canceled` and `void` runs are recorded with their reasons, both in the run result and in the slot's retained output artifact (`panel-slot-output`, referenced by `outputArtifact`). A failed slot is never retried or replaced by a fallback. Harnesses may report `observed: { harnessVersion?, model?, accountIdentity?, disallowedTools?, usage? }` on their output. Values they do not report are taken from preflight or configuration, and usage is never estimated.
- **Quorum.** Within a stage, the first completed run of an identity counts and later completed runs of that identity are `collapsed`. A stage with fewer counted runs than its quorum makes coverage incomplete with a reason starting `REVIEWFN_PANEL_QUORUM_UNMET`, so the verdict cannot be `ready`.
- **Union.** Each completed or collapsed slot's findings are validated alone against the panel contract. An invalid finding is excluded with a coverage reason that names its slot, so it cannot remove another slot's valid finding. Every remaining finding enters the report, even when only one slot reported it. Findings with the same fingerprint merge: their origins, evidence and highest severity are kept. Agreement is recorded in `origins` and `confidence` (the share of contributing slots) and never filters a finding. Evidence IDs are prefixed with the slot ID. The requirements slot's findings also join the union, except `info` findings, which stay in its requirements report. Changed paths that no contributing slot inspected (delta paths in delta mode) make coverage incomplete.
- **Requirements.** The requirements slot uses the 0.1 prompt and schema over the full change, plus its lens. Its 0.1 report is built by the shared 0.1 report path; a run that does not count yields a report whose execution did not complete.
- **Delta mode.** With `incremental: "delta"` and `since`, lens slots receive the delta hunks as their primary scope and the full change and hunks as reference. Requirements are always assessed against the full change.
- **Report.** The panel report is validated with `validatePanelReport` against the run's frozen context, artifacts, source control and panel policy, and is stored as a `panel-report` artifact. If validation finds issues, the report is still stored, with coverage incomplete, the issues as coverage reasons, and the verdict re-derived. Panel output stays advisory.

---

<!-- page:docs:reference/report-schema.md path:/docs/reference/report-schema -->
# Report schema

> Execution, coverage, verdict, assessments, evidence, and findings.


A report records three independent axes:

- execution: `queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, or `superseded`;
- coverage: `complete` or `incomplete`, with reasons;
- verdict: `ready`, `changes_requested`, or `needs_verification`, absent unless execution is `completed`; a completed run without complete coverage or requirements is `needs_verification`.

Requirements contain immutable source anchors and exactly one assessment. Assessments distinguish `implemented`, `partial`, `missing`, `unverified`, and source-waived `not_applicable`. Evidence links to a context source, exact-head code anchor, diff, test receipt, or content-addressed artifact. An implemented assessment must include reviewed-head implementation evidence. Merge-base anchors can document deleted code but cannot alone establish implementation. An available source with no extracted requirements needs explicit source evidence with a nonblank `sourceExclusionReason`; ordinary citations do not establish exclusion.

Findings carry a fingerprint, severity, concrete trigger/impact/direction, reproduced-versus-inferred basis, requirement links and lifecycle. Model confidence never substitutes for evidence validity. Fingerprints use path, optional symbol and finding semantics, excluding revision and line coordinates. They are correlation hints, not proof of historical lifecycle. Version 0.1 receives no prior-finding provenance, so only `new` findings validate; every historical lifecycle remains unproven. Ambiguous duplicate fingerprints fail validation; distinguish actual symbols or defect semantics before correlation.

`contextManifestDigest` identifies the normalized snapshot bytes and `contextManifestArtifact` names the corresponding content-addressed stored artifact. Test receipts contain exact argv, commit, timing, exit status, stdout/stderr digests and limitations; they do not claim a retrievable log artifact unless one was actually persisted.

`changeDetail` is optional and additive; a report without it validates as before. When present, `hunksArtifact` names a content-addressed `change-hunks` artifact whose SHA-256 is `hunksDigest`. The artifact is a `ChangeHunks` v1 document, `{ version: 1, baseCommit, headCommit, files: [{ path, previousPath?, status, hunks: [{ oldStart, oldLines, newStart, newLines }] }] }`, parsed from `git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --find-renames -U0 <mergeBase> <head>`. `status` is `added`, `modified`, `deleted`, `renamed` or `binary`. Binary files have no hunks, and the report lists them as limitations because they cannot carry line-level evidence. Diffs larger than the policy's `maxOutputBytes` are not parsed: the report omits `changeDetail` and records incomplete coverage with the reason. The same holds when the artifact store refuses the hunks artifact. Combined diffs, word diffs and external diff drivers are rejected (`REVIEWFN_DIFF_UNSUPPORTED`).

An incremental run sets `since` to the previously reviewed head, a full 40- or 64-hex commit. `since` must be an ancestor of the head and a descendant of, or equal to, the merge base. Otherwise the run fails before review with `REVIEWFN_SINCE_NOT_ANCESTOR`, and it never falls back to a full review. The report then also records `deltaHunksArtifact` and `deltaHunksDigest` for `since..head`, plus `deltaPaths`, the delta's changed paths. Like every changed path, each delta path must be inspected or explicitly uninspected. A delta path that the verified delta removes but the full change never lists (a file added after the merge base and deleted by a later push) is inspected at `since`; code and finding anchors may cite `since` only for such removed paths. The validator recomputes both digests from the stored artifacts and checks their commit ranges and paths against the change. Any mismatch fails with `REVIEWFN_CHANGE_DETAIL_MISMATCH`.

The validator rejects duplicate identifiers, unknown requirements/evidence/sources, stale commit anchors, invalid line ranges, unjustified exclusions, over-limit findings, incomplete-ready reports and any verdict inconsistent with deterministic policy.

---

<!-- page:docs:reference/security.md path:/docs/reference/security -->
# Security model

> Trust boundaries, Docker containment, credentials, and retention.


The trusted boundary contains the pinned installation, base-revision policy, context collector, coordinator and separate publisher. Repository files, retrieved text, test output and model output are untrusted.

The CLI clones the committed target into an owned independent checkout. Mutable tracked and untracked caller files are excluded. The source adapter independently rejects dirty review roots. Configuration is loaded from the immutable base revision in CI; a PR cannot select its own executable, commands or limits. Global execution configuration must be controlled by the runner administrator.

Tests require Docker; there is no host-execution fallback. The pinned Node 22 image runs with no network, no capabilities, no privilege escalation, a read-only root, an unprivileged UID, 1 CPU, 512 MiB memory, 128 PIDs, a 256 MiB workspace and 64 MiB temporary filesystem. Input archives are bounded at 256 MiB. Only the committed archive is mounted read-only; no home directory, credentials, source checkout, Docker socket or host output directory is available to tests. The entire container is removed on every terminal path, including successful parents with detached descendants. Commands share a batch deadline and have bounded output. Dependencies must be present in the trusted image or committed input; commands cannot install them over the network.

PR inference requires action-proxy authentication and the trusted `reviewfn-codex:0.154.0` image. Build its packaged Dockerfile before running. The review checkout is read-only; only a fresh owned result directory is writable on the host. CPU, memory, PID, temporary disk, runtime and output limits also apply to inference. The proxy endpoint provides inference access only; it must not embed a raw provider credential. The container has outbound networking for this proxy and receives no publication token or host home directory. Restrict its egress at the runner/network layer where repository confidentiality requires a single allowed destination.

Codex disables project-document loading and user config. Changes to `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.override.md`, `.codex/`, `.agents/`, or `.claude/` fail before inference. API-key and ChatGPT modes are available only for trusted local reviews without a PR identity. Access-token and workload-identity modes currently fail explicit compatibility preflight. There is no automatic authentication fallback.

The review CLI refuses a process environment containing `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Publication uses a separate trusted job and a retained report, without running repository code or inference. Use a per-repository/PR/profile concurrency group for cross-run serialization. Head checks occur after comment discovery and before comment/check writes. GitHub does not provide a transaction spanning head changes and comment creation; a race after a check is reported stale, and every comment names its reviewed SHA. Checks remain neutral.

Artifact filenames and metadata identities are validated. Reads and writes reject target and parent symlinks, apart from known root-owned macOS system aliases. Atomic private output writes occur outside the untrusted execution boundary. Retention validates matching metadata IDs before deletion. Tests retain redacted logs; transcripts require `retainTranscript: true`; events and all harness output are redacted using both detected secrets and the explicitly configured credential value. The CLI applies retention cleanup when saving a new run. Operators must schedule `new FileArtifactStore(artifactsDirectory, outputDirectory).deleteExpired()` for idle stores; the optional second directory includes CLI report.json/report.md copies in expiry cleanup. Shared content keeps the longest active expiration, including imports from run workspaces. Store mutations serialize through .retention.lock; after a crashed writer, the lock records PID, hostname, and acquisition time. Remove it only after confirming the owning process is dead on the recorded host; never reclaim an ambiguous or active owner automatically. Exports changed outside ReviewFn are preserved with a cleanup error rather than deleted. Failed copy writes retain expiry coverage for both old and proposed bytes; cleanup also removes content-addressed data orphaned before its metadata commit. The CLI saves the new review outputs but exits nonzero with REVIEWFN_RETENTION_CLEANUP_FAILED when cleanup reports errors.

Public forks never receive repository secrets. A proxy and isolated runner must be deliberately provisioned before enabling reviews. The publisher must download only the artifact from its trusted review job and verify PR/head/profile against event metadata. Never execute a PR-owned workflow, package or image with publication credentials.

Linked Linear document URLs must share the server-returned issue URL workspace, and returned canonical document URLs are rechecked before their content enters review context. Issue-attached document records inherit their verified issue association. Missing optional Markdown globs are accepted as empty selections; use an exact file path when absence must make context incomplete.

Host snapshot checkout, source capture, and test archive preparation use credential-free Git environments with system/global configuration disabled; checkout also disables templates, hooks, and global attributes. Reproduced findings require a completed reviewed-head test receipt and retained logs whose digests verify. Requirement text alone cannot substantiate a defect finding.

Deleted changed paths may use verified merge-base code anchors only when the source adapter proves the path is absent from the head. Existing paths still require head-commit anchors.


Native tool lookup on Windows resolves `.exe` binaries and rejects repository-owned paths; shell-dependent `.cmd`/`.bat` wrappers are not supported. POSIX world-write and execute-bit checks apply only on POSIX. Windows operators must provision PATH directories with trusted ACLs: Node's `stat.mode` does not validate Windows ACL ownership. Native Windows executable-name handling has regression-test coverage by simulating `process.platform` on POSIX. The full consumer and Docker gates remain verified on POSIX, not Windows end to end.

Normalized Codex telemetry is capped at 10,000 retained events including a truncation warning. If the limit is reached, successful inference still records incomplete telemetry scope, while timeout and cancellation outcomes retain their terminal state.

---

<!-- page:docs:security.md path:/docs/security -->
# Security and isolation

> Prepare the trusted runner, containers, credentials, and output boundary.


Treat repository files, issue text, test output, and model output as untrusted. The trusted boundary contains the installed CLI, base-revision policy, context collector, coordinator, and separate publisher. In CI, pass `--trusted-config-from-base` so a PR cannot change the policy or executable that evaluates itself.

Tests require a pinned Docker image with no network, no credentials, a read-only root, an unprivileged UID, and fixed CPU, memory, process, disk, and time limits. There is no host-execution fallback. PR inference requires the trusted `reviewfn-codex:0.154.0` image and an inference-only proxy; it must not receive a raw provider or GitHub publication token. Build that image from the packaged harness Dockerfile and provision the proxy before enabling reviews.

The review CLI refuses `GITHUB_TOKEN` in its environment. Put publication in a separate trusted job that reads a retained report and verifies the PR, head, and profile from event metadata. The CLI rejects changed auto-loaded agent instruction and configuration paths before inference. Locally trusted API-key and ChatGPT modes are not PR inference modes.

The [full security model](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/security.md) records exact bounds, redaction, artifact retention, symlink protection, platform caveats, and cleanup rules. Review it before running against untrusted code.

---

<!-- page:docs:workflow.md path:/docs/workflow -->
# Review workflow

> Follow exact revisions from context capture to validated report.


ReviewFn identifies the base, head, merge-base, diff, configuration, policy, prompt, harness, model, and budget for each run. It freezes authoritative issue and repository context before inference. A source adapter rejects a dirty review root, while the CLI clones committed input into its own checkout so mutable caller files are excluded.

Approved test commands are argv arrays, not shell scripts. The test adapter runs them in a bounded Docker container against a committed archive. The review harness receives the frozen evidence and returns structured assessments and findings. The validator checks source IDs, requirements, exact-head code anchors, test receipts, evidence links, severity, and verdict consistency before a report can be ready.

Every extracted requirement resolves to exactly one assessment. The report separates execution (`completed`, `failed`, and other states), coverage (`complete` or `incomplete`), and verdict (`ready`, `changes_requested`, or `needs_verification`). A completed model call alone does not imply a valid review. Once execution starts, missing context, malformed output, timeout, quota, cancellation, or stale-head outcomes remain visible in the report. Preflight failures such as unsupported authentication are returned as diagnostics and stop the run before a report is created.

Use the [report schema](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/report-schema.md) for field-level rules and [security model](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/security.md) for checkout, test, and inference isolation. To compare review quality, run [frozen evaluations](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/evaluation.md) and retain their limitations.

---
